claims: A heat dome is caused by a persistent, high-pressure system that settles over a region.
A heat dome acts as a "lid" on a pot.
A heat dome traps hot air.
A heat dome prevents cloud formation.
A heat dome forces air to sink and compress.
A strong, high-pressure ridge in the upper atmosphere pushes warm air toward the ground.
As the air sinks, it warms.
Sinking air creates a "dome" of trapped heat.
High pressure suppresses cloud formation.
High pressure suppresses precipitation.
The area experiences sunny skies.
The area experiences very little wind.
The area experiences increasing temperatures.
Heat domes can last for days or even weeks.
Heat domes result in building, compounding temperatures that provide little relief at night.
Heat domes cause severe heat waves (100°F+).
Heat domes accelerate drought conditions.
Heat domes pose significant risks to public health particularly in regions not acclimated to extreme heat.
The high-pressure system keeps hot air trapped near the surface.
Heat domes are often linked to changes in the jet stream.
Heat domes are becoming more intense and frequent due to climate change.
